summary: Anagarika Munindra worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka, and served as superintendent at the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.
Active in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, Anam Thubten Rinpoche studied under the traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche. He held a post as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

Anand A. Yang works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Swarthmore College (~1966–1970) and the University of Virginia (~1970–1976), he held posts at Sweet Briar College, the University of Utah, and the University of Washington.

Anand Venkatkrishnan is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at Columbia University by 2015 and was attested in 2026 as Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago.

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy was an Indology, history, archaeology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Wycliffe College, University College London, and under Caroline Rhys Davids. He directed Ceylon's Geological Survey and held posts at the Boston MFA and the Smithsonian.

Ananda W. P. Guruge worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Ceylon and University of London. He held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and the University of the West.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), the Numismatic Society of India (1947), Patna University (~1949–1957), and the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts as a professor at the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research (~1955–1974) and as director at the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds, later serving as professor of religion at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

Andrea Acri is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied under Raffaele Torella, Arlo Griffiths, and Willem van der Molen, earning a PhD from Leiden University. He held positions at Leiden University and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Andrea R. Jain is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD 2010), holding posts at the University of Houston, Rice University, IUPUI, and Indiana University Bloomington, where she became professor.

Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Richard G. Salomon and Ingo Strauch, earning degrees from the Free University of Berlin, and holds posts attested in 2026 at Göttingen Academy and the University of Munich.

Andreas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, studied under traditional teachers Chokyi Nyima, Tsikey Chokling, and Phakchok Rinpoche, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
Andreas Spengel was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at the University of Munich (~1856–1859) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1859–1861).

Andree Dominique Messent specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Messent completed a PhD at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Paul Williams, also studying under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. After completing a PhD at Boston University, he held a post as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College, attested in 2009.
Andrew Garrett is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard University from ~1983 to 1990 and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1995.

Andrew Glass specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA, PhD), supervised by Richard G. Salomon and taught by Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Wanggyal Sonam, and Gudrun Melzer.

Andrew Goudie specializes in history and archaeology. He studied at Dean Close School (~1958–1963) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1964–1969), and served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.
Andrew Huxley was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at SOAS University of London in 1984 and as attested in 1996.
